newsitem.title: UK: London & Manchester sees good start to 1997.
newsitem.headline: London & Manchester sees good start to 1997.

text.p: Life and corporate pensions company London & Manchester Group Plc said on Tuesday that its home service business had made a good start to the year.

"The major investment we have made in our life assurance business over the past three years evidences our commitment to the home service market," chairman David Hubbard and chief executive Tom Payne said in a statement accompanying results.

The company last year completed a large-scale programme to re-engineer its homes service sales operation, changes which it said had made a "material effect" on the division's new business results in 1996.

This restructuring was completed in the fourth quarter of 1996 with the opening of the last of its 18 business centres. While these changes affected sales results, there were signs as the year closed that the disruption was coming to an end. Home service new business levels stabilised in the second half of 1996 and the early evidence for 1997 was encouraging.

"It is...particularly pleasing to enter 1997 with these major changes behind us and with early evidence of a very encouraging increase in sales force productivity and new business levels," the statement said.
New sales teams in personal financial services had been trained to a high standard to meet customer needs.

"We anticipate that the potential of our new sales and service teams will begin to be realised in 1997, with the returning confidence of the personal saver and the country's favourable economic conditions contributing positively to our new business results," chairman David Hubbard said.

On the corporate pensions side, the focus for 1997 would remain on tailor-made solutions and providing technical back-up, especially in helping clients through the ramifications of the Pensions Act, it said.

The company reported a 10.8 percent rise in distributable profits to 39.5 million stg in the year to December 31, from 35.7 million the year before. It proposed a total dividend of 20.29 pence a share, up 8.5 percent from the previous year's 18.90 pence.
